elements_not_encoded.text: First assess and manage airway, breathing, circulation and level of consciousness 16.
elements_not_encoded.reason: ABC assessment instruction with pointer to page 16; no triage criterion.

elements_not_encoded.text: Identify all injuries and look for cause. Undress patient and assess front and back. If head or spine injury, use log-roll to turn. Then cover and keep warm.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Examination and handling instruction (undress, log-roll, keep warm).

elements_not_encoded.text: Give sodium chloride 0.9% 1L IV hourly for 2 hours, then 500mL hourly. Aim for urine output > 200mL/hour. Stop if breathing worsens.
elements_not_encoded.reason: IV fluid regimen for bruising with blood in urine.

elements_not_encoded.text: If shock1/SBP < 80, give sodium chloride 0.9% 1L IV rapidly, repeat until systolic BP > 80. Continue 1L 6 hourly. Stop if breathing worsens.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Fluid resuscitation for shock/SBP < 80; the shock definition itself is encoded from footnote 1.

elements_not_encoded.text: If pain severe, give morphine 5-10mg IM or 3-5mg slow IV2. Avoid if severe head injury.
If poor perfusion, weakness/numbness below fracture, gently re-align into normal position.
If GCS < 15, neck/spine tenderness, weak/numb limb or abnormal pupils, apply rigid neck collar and sandbags/ blocks on either side of head.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Spinal immobilisation; its conditions (GCS < 15, neck/spine tenderness) only gate the collar, not urgency.

elements_not_encoded.text: If excessive or pulsatile bleeding, apply direct pressure and elevate limb.
If open fracture, remove foreign material, irrigate with sodium chloride 0.9% and cover with saline-soaked gauze. Discuss antibiotic management with referral ho
elements_not_encoded.reason: Open fracture wound care and antibiotic discussion.

elements_not_encoded.text: If pupils unequal or respond poorly to light, keep body straight and tilt to raise head (avoid bending spine).
If bleeding severe and persists, apply tourniquet above injury.
Splint limb to immobilise joint above and below fracture.
If pelvic fracture, tie sheet tightly around hips to immobilise.

elements_not_encoded.reason: Pointer to seizure page 20; seizure itself is encoded as a head-injury sign.

elements_not_encoded.text: Refer urgently. While awaiting transport, check BP, pulse, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation and GCS every 15 minutes.
If open wound, suture as below and give tetanus toxoid 0.5mL IM if none in past 5 years.
If BP < 90/60, pulse > 100 or < 50, respiratory rate > 20 or < 9, oxygen saturation < 94% or drop in GCS, reassess airway, breathing, circulation, level of cons
elements_not_encoded.reason: Reassessment triggers (BP < 90/60, pulse, RR, SpO2, GCS) during monitoring of an already urgent patient; routes to page 16, does not add urgency criteria.

judgment_calls.decision: One Urgent priority rule per group (bruising + blood in urine; wound; fracture; head injury), each (and <group finding> (or <signs>)), plus one check_for task per group triggered by the group finding.
judgment_calls.alternatives: A single priority rule with an or of four ands.

judgment_calls.decision: Traumatic injury (disorder), the concept the VHA warning-sign table already records. Wound, Fracture of bone and Injury of head are not SNOMED descendants of it, so each has its own task.
judgment_calls.alternatives: Traumatic or non-traumatic injury (the common parent).

judgment_calls.decision: Probable Shock if injured and any one of SBP < 80, pulse >= 100, RR > 30, confusion, restlessness, weakness.
judgment_calls.alternatives: All of them, or any two; the page does not say.
Persistent vomiting (narrower), or not encoding it.

judgment_calls.topic: Increasing pain, muscle tightness, numbness in limb
judgment_calls.decision: Any one sign (or); muscle tightness has no SNOMED concept and is not encoded.

Any of Limb ischemia (the named sign), Cold extremity ('cold'), Numbness of limbs ('numb') or Peripheral pulse absent ('no pulse'); 'pale' has no limb concept; 'below' not expressible. Merged from builders A and B.
judgment_calls.alternatives: Only Limb ischemia + absent pulse (builder A), or only the listed signs (builder B).

judgment_calls.decision: Or of Fracture of three/four/five/six/seven/eight OR more ribs.
Nasal discharge / Ear discharge with the Clear qualifier, as the page words it.
judgment_calls.alternatives: Cerebrospinal fluid rhinorrhea/otorrhea (builder B; an interpretation the page does not state).

judgment_calls.decision: Sluggish pupil movement or No pupillary reaction to light.
judgment_calls.alternatives: Abnormal pupil reaction (builder B); its only child in SNOMED is poor dilation to mydriatic drops, so it does not mean the light response.
